summary: #341 consolidation. Materialized/read ST I q.2 a.3 (quarta via), ST I q.44 a.1 and In Metaph. II lect. 2 in full. Derived STMT-GRADES-HAVE-A-MAXIMUM by well-founded induction along distinct causes of a perfection from four nonlogical premises plus excluded middle: more-such-has-the-perfection (read from q.2 a.3, exceeding side only), the existing unrestricted cause-more-such (already on the Fourth Way root route), exceeded-is-caused (unattributed; q.44 a.1 supports it at esse via participation, does not state it) and no infinite regress of causes of a perfection (In Metaph. II l.2 n.11, reading step: line indexed by perfection rather than species of cause). One Boolean omission fixture per premise. Considered and set aside: (A) the order-only route, bearer premise plus ascending well-foundedness of MoreIn itself, which is shorter but its well-foundedness premise has no source read here (no text denies an infinite ascent of degrees as such); (B) Zorn's chain-bound condition, which on a homogeneous scale suffices (zornMaximum) and is weaker than ascending well-foundedness, but presupposes an order on degrees that Aquinas' analogical reading does not supply and still needs its own existence premise (every chain bounded on the scale). Maximal versus greatest: directedness plus antisymmetry make a maximal grade the unique greatest one (directedMaximalIsGreatest); without them INFINITE-GREATEST-WHOLE-CONTROL and MaximumNeedNotBeUnique already give incomparable or tied maxima. Rejected: an approach-to-a-maximum premise that presupposes the maximum (a transcription of the conclusion). Not done: target 4's first-cause-is-maximal with Acc, formal versus virtual containment, and the mapping of the other two frontier premises. Because GRADES is sourced, the root-route cost cannot fall by this derivation alone (corpus.py root_routes); it moves the closure burden to the four premises.
